newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends sharply down on dollar build-ups.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends sharply down on dollar build-ups.

text.p: The won closed sharply lower against the dollar on Thursday as dollar demand strengthened in views that the U.S. unit was undervalued, dealers said.
"Dollar demand shot up in expectations of a further rise," said a domestic bank dealer.
The won closed at 893.90 after opening at 890.00. It briefly touched 894.60, the lowest since the country launched the market average system in March 1990.
Dealers said lack of a central bank dollar sales in the spot trading boosted buying of the dollar.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 893.50 on Friday, compared with 889.50 today.
Dealers said the shrinking foreign currency reserves at the Bank of Korea hampered its direct intervention.
The reserves fell to around $25 billion won now from about $30 billion at the end of February, they said.
A domestic bank dealer forecast a range of 890.00 to 895.00 on Friday, while a foreign bank dealer put it between 891.00 to 896.00.
